: dog body extension = 0.5 + weight/20 = 0.5 + 15/20 = 1.25 m, maximum reach = 1.5 + 1.25 = 2.75 m. City coefficient 0.6 -> safe distance 1.65 m; braking distance = 2.75 × 0.3 × 1.0 (normal reaction) = 0.82 m; controllable net distance = 1.65 − 0.82 ≈ 0.82 m. That is, in an urban environment the actual controllable range is only about 0.8 m, so walk close or switch to a shorter leash. For comparison, the park coefficient of 1.0 gives a controllable net distance of 1.93 m, the crowd coefficient of 0.4 only 0.28 m, and a trail coefficient of 0.7 gives 1.1 m.
map.为什么公园和人群的系数差这么多？: Why do the park and crowd coefficients differ so much?
map.公园开阔、突发干扰少，可达范围可放至 1.0；人群密集时犬只易受惊扰冲撞，系数降: Parks are open with few sudden distractions, so the reachable range can go to 1.0; in dense crowds dogs startle and bolt easily, so the coefficient drops to 0.4 to force a shorter effective distance, pressing the controllable net distance to about 0.3 m and requiring close control by the owner.
